figures.name: fig01_paired_quality
figures.title: Sample-Aligned Classification Comparison
figures.caption: Fixed prompt v1 and threshold 0.5; F1 and AUROC are shown per dataset. Within each dataset, all models use exactly the same successful sample IDs, unlike the multi-model reference pages, which use each model's own successful samples. The dotted 50% line in the AUROC panel is the random-ranking baseline. No confidence intervals are shown.

figures.name: fig02_quality_cost_tradeoff
figures.title: Error Rates and Latency Trade-offs
figures.caption: Lower-left is better in the left panel, which uses all shared baseline datasets. Upper-left is better in the right panel, which uses only shared datasets with complete v1 / 0.5 timing for every model; both macro AUROC and sample-weighted elapsed time are recomputed on that same subset. The dataset scopes may differ between panels and are stated in the figure. Four-run average timing never substitutes for missing single-run timing. Elapsed time includes network overhead and waits for failed requests; it is not pure inference latency or P95. Timing is N/A when no shared fully timed subset exists.

figures.name: fig03_threshold_sensitivity
figures.title: Prompt and Threshold Sensitivity (Fastino, Laya, TypeSafe)
figures.caption: Colors identify models; solid lines with circles indicate v1, and dashed lines with triangles indicate v2. Filled markers use shared successful samples at the same configuration. When paired metrics are unavailable, hollow markers show the model's own successful samples, so missing results from another model do not hide available measurements. Missing or all-failed configurations remain gaps, without zero-filling or interpolation. Sample sets may differ across points; this is not a fair ranking. Each threshold requires a new model call, so the curves mix threshold effects with repeat-call variation rather than isolating threshold effects on fixed scores. This is exploration on the same test set, not an independently validated performance improvement.

figures.name: fig04_evaluation_coverage
figures.title: Evaluation Coverage and Request Failures
figures.caption: Coverage is successful samples / reference samples. Gray indicates an unavailable prediction file; hatching indicates a fully saved run in which every request failed. PII is ordinary binary classification (PII present vs absent); rows show coverage, not masking quality. Missing Laya results are not scored as zero.

figures.name: fig05_dataset_metrics
figures.title: Per-Dataset Performance Metrics (Fastino, Laya, TypeSafe)
figures.caption: Fixed prompt v1 and threshold 0.5; Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1, AUROC and average latency (ms) are shown for all datasets. Quality metrics use each model's own successful samples, not a fair sample-aligned ranking; request errors are excluded from quality scores. PII is ordinary binary classification (PII present vs absent), not entity extraction or masking quality; the current positives-only labels make AUROC undefined. Elapsed time is elapsed / processed from complete, matched logs, including network overhead and failure waits. Missing results, no successful predictions, undefined metrics or incomplete timing are N/A, never zero-filled. A run with all requests failed may still have recorded elapsed time.

figures.name: fig06_model_averages
figures.title: Sample-Aligned Model Averages (Fastino, Laya, TypeSafe)
figures.caption: Fixed prompt v1 and threshold 0.5; average Accuracy, Precision, Recall, AUROC and latency (ms) are reported for jointly completed non-PII datasets with shared successful samples. Classification metrics are computed on shared successful samples, then averaged equally across datasets. Latency also gives equal weight to each dataset's full-run average, but uses only the shared baseline subset with complete v1 / 0.5 timing for every model. All models use exactly the same timing dataset scope. Quality and timing scopes may differ; actual counts and timing datasets are stated in the figure. Four-run averages never substitute for missing single-run timing. This differs from the sample-weighted timing in Figure 2. Latency is N/A only when there is no shared fully timed subset.

figures.name: fig07_repeat_consistency_v1
figures.title: Repeat-Call Consistency: v1 (Fastino, Laya, TypeSafe)
figures.caption: Only datasets with all four rounds complete for every model and shared successful samples are shown. Within each dataset, every model uses the same samples that succeeded in all four calls for all models. Lower mean population standard deviation of scores, mean score range and decision-flip rate at a fixed threshold of 0.5 indicate greater consistency. The first two metrics are multiplied by 100 in the figure; original scores range from 0 to 1. Shared four-round success coverage and each model's request failure rate are also shown. Datasets with missing rounds or no shared successful samples are excluded. Measured zeros use baseline markers; they are not missing or imputed values. Consistency does not imply correctness, and historical service changes may also affect results.

figures.name: fig08_repeat_consistency_v2
figures.title: Repeat-Call Consistency: v2 (Fastino, Laya, TypeSafe)
figures.caption: As for v1, only datasets with four complete rounds for every model and shared successful samples are shown. Metrics use samples shared by all models; v2 is analyzed separately. The four raw scores are compared directly, with decisions uniformly defined as score >= 0.5, rather than comparing prediction columns produced at different CSV thresholds. Four calls provide exploratory evidence only; differences cannot be attributed entirely to model randomness. Zero values use baseline markers and mean measured stability, not missing data. Coverage uses samples successful across all models and all four rounds; failure rates use each model's complete saved requests for those datasets.

figures.name: fig09_repeat_consistency_averages
figures.title: Repeat-Call Consistency Averages (Fastino, Laya, TypeSafe)
figures.caption: v1 and v2 are analyzed separately. Each dataset requires four complete rounds for every model and uses the same samples that succeeded for all models in all four calls. Metrics are then averaged equally across non-PII datasets with shared successful samples. Lower values indicate greater consistency for all three metrics. Shared datasets or samples may differ between prompts. If no shared dataset is available, the result is N/A. Measured zeros use baseline markers and are neither missing nor imputed. See the full report and CSV files for raw metrics, shared sample counts, coverage and failure rates.
